# requireNumberLike

<link-summary>Returns the value as a numeric value, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNumberLike() — Returns the value as a numeric value, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNumberLike(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a numeric value."
): number | string;
```

A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                              | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a numeric value."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number | string` — the same value, typed as a numeric value.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                 |
| :------------------------- | :---------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not convertible to a number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNumberLike(1); // => 1
requireNumberLike("1.5"); // => "1.5"
requireNumberLike(NaN); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNumberLike(Infinity); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
